chunks: I wrote to Abu Ja'far (the second) [peace be upon him]: The narrations regarding the completion (full prayer) and shortening (reduced prayer) of the prayer in the two Sanctuaries have differed from your fathers (peace be upon him). Some command completing the prayer even if it is a single prayer, and some command shortening the prayer as long as one does not intend to stay for ten days. I remained upon the completion in both until we departed from our Hajj this year, and the jurists of our companions advised me to shorten [the prayer] if I do not intend to stay for ten days. I became constrained by this, so I sought your opinion. He wrote in his own hand: 'You know, may God have mercy on you, the virtue of prayer in the two Sanctuaries over others than them. So I love for you, when you enter them, not to shorten [the prayer] and to increase in them from the prayer.' I said to him after that, two years later, in person: 'I wrote to you such-and-such, and you answered with such-and-such.' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'What do you mean by the two Sanctuaries?' He said: 'Mecca and Medina. And when you head from Mina, shorten the prayer. And when you return from Arafat to Mina, and visit the House, and return to Mina, complete the prayer for those three days.' And he indicated with his finger [saying] three.

key_terms.الإِتمَام: Completion (performing four-rak'ah prayers in places where two are usually performed)
key_terms.البَيت: The House (referring to the Kaaba in Mecca)
key_terms.التّقصِير: Shortening (performing two-rak'ah prayers in places where four are usually performed)
key_terms.الحَرَمَين: The two Sanctuaries (referring to Mecca and Medina)
key_terms.عَرَفَات: Arafat (the plain where the standing during Hajj takes place)
key_terms.مِنًي: Mina (a location near Mecca significant for Hajj rituals)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on shortening or completing prayers in Mecca and Medina during Hajj according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This correspondence highlights the scholarly nuance between the general virtue of completing prayers in the Sanctuaries (al-Haramayn) and the specific ritual practice during Hajj, where the Imam instructs shortening prayers upon leaving Mina but completing them during the days of Tashriq after visiting the Kaaba. It reflects the Shia jurisprudential approach of distinguishing between permanent sanctity and temporary ritual states, resolving the discrepancy among earlier Imams by linking the ruling to the pilgrim's movement and intention. This hadith is pivotal in establishing the distinct Shia position on prayer length in Mecca and Medina compared to other Islamic schools.
